newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close higher as power stocks shine.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close higher as power stocks shine.

text.p: Chilean blue chips, led by electricity shares, closed more than one percent higher on Monday, as heavy weekend rain eased fears of power rationing, traders said.
"It's all due to the fact that it's rained down south and the risk of rationing is disappearing very quickly," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
The surge is seen resuming at Tuesday's opening, with power stocks expected to extend their rally, he said.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended up 1.04 percent at 121.1 points.
The general .IGPA index gained 0.47 percent to 5,382.19 points.
Turnover rose to 14.9 billion pesos -- its highest level in over a week -- from a thin seven billion pesos Friday.
Leading gainers included hydroelectric generators, whose earnings have fallen sharply amid a drought that has forced them to buy expensive power on the spot market.
More rain is expected in coming days and that should drive power stocks even higher, Hurd said.
Enersis climbed 2.13 percent to 263-1/2 pesos, while Endesa was up 1.94 percent at 263 pesos.
Endesa also benefited from optimism that its earnings will show a sharp improvement next year as new dams, including the huge Pague project, are completed, traders said
Decliners included glass-maker Cristales, down 3.85 percent at 3,000, and drug producer LabChile, which shed 1.02 percent at 485 pesos.
